chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah be pleased with him) said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar said: al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf narrated from Sa'dan ibn Muslim, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
I heard him saying: One is only argued with (in matters of faith) if he lacks piety or if he is a man of doubt.
ai.seo_question: Why do people argue in matters of faith according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In *Al-Tawhid*, Shaykh al-Saduq records Imam al-Sadiq (AS) identifying two primary archetypes of theological debaters: the impious who argue for dominance, and the doubtful who argue from uncertainty. This hadith serves as a foundational critique in Shia scholarship of *Kalam* (speculative theology) when it becomes an end in itself, distinguishing between genuine understanding and mere verbal contention. It underscores that true knowledge is rooted in *War'* (piety/consciousness of God), whereas excessive argumentation often signals a lack of spiritual certainty.

en.sayed-ali-raza-rizvi: 23. Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (RA) said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan alSaffar said: al-`Abbas ibn Ma`ruf said, on the authority of Sa`dan ibn Muslim, on the authority of Abu Basir that Abu `Abd Allah al-Sadiq (AS) said:
“The only ones who quarrel in matters of faith are those who lack piety or who are assailed by doubts.”
